lines: Sermon theme — Mercy that will not be sent away

verses: From heaven you came, helpless babe,
entered our world, your glory veiled;
not to be served, but to serve,
and give your life that we might live.
This is our God, the Servant King,
he calls us now to follow him,
to bring our lives as a daily offering
of worship to the Servant King.
There in the garden of tears,
my heavy load he chose to bear;
his heart with sorrow was torn,
‘Yet not my will, but yours’ he said.
This is our God, the Servant King,
he calls us now to follow him,
to bring our lives as a daily offering
of worship to the Servant King.
Come see his hands and his feet,
the scars that speak of sacrifice,
hands that flung stars into space
to cruel nails surrendered.
This is our God, the Servant King,
he calls us now to follow him,
to bring our lives as a daily offering
of worship to the Servant King.
So let us learn how to serve
and in our lives enthrone him;
each other’s needs to prefer,
for it is Christ we’re serving.
This is our God, the Servant King,
he calls us now to follow him,
to bring our lives as a daily offering
of worship to the Servant King.

blocks.call: We are gathered in the name of God.

lines: Come, let us gather at the table of freedom.
Come, lift your voices in praise to God.
Come, bring your hope and your struggle, your courage and your pain.
We come, for all are welcome in Christ’s presence.
The Spirit of the Lord is upon us—
to lift the lowly, to break the chains.
Rise in body or in spirit, and let us worship.
For God is here, setting people free.
Before the God who makes us one,
we confess the ways we have sown division and withheld peace.
Come, bring your burdens and brokenness,
for in Christ mercy and reconciliation are offered to all.
we admit that we have done wrong:
in our thoughts, words, and actions.
and guide us in the future.
and to walk humbly with you.
God, the Source of mercy and renewal,
forgives you and sets you free.
Christ restores you in his likeness,
that your life may reflect love and goodness.
The Holy Spirit strengthens you to walk the way of justice and peace.
We give thanks to you, gracious God,
for your mercy restores and your grace makes us whole.
You have drawn near in every age—
freeing the captives, forgiving the broken, feeding the hungry.
From the beginning you made the world in goodness,
a gift of grace where salvation is written in every living thing.
In Jesus, your Word became flesh,
bringing salvation to the world and grace upon grace.
By your Spirit, you breathe life into our weary souls
and set us again on the path of joy.
We give you thanks and praise,

blocks.text: Transition to the readings: Mercy that will not be sent away

paragraphs: Today from the Bible we will hear two stories about mercy that refuses to be narrowed.
From Paul’s letter to the Romans — God’s gifts and calling cannot be taken back. Whatever we have made of each other, God has not written anybody off.
From Matthew’s gospel — a foreign woman who will not be silenced, who argues with Jesus about the size of the table, and who wins.

lines: Open our ears to the word that is near us.
A reading from the letter of Paul to the Romans.

paragraphs: So I ask you, has God rejected his people? Absolutely not! I’m an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin. God hasn’t rejected his people, whom he knew in advance. Or don’t you know what the scripture says in the case of Elijah, when he pleads with God against Israel?

God’s gifts and calling can’t be taken back. Once you were disobedient to God, but now you have mercy because they were disobedient. In the same way, they have also been disobedient because of the mercy that you received, so now they can receive mercy too. God has locked up all people in disobedience, in order to have mercy on all of them.

blocks.call: This is the word of the Lord

segments: Great is your faith; let it be done for you as you wish.

blocks.call: A reading from the Good News according to Matthew.
blocks.response: Glory to you Lord Jesus Christ

paragraphs: From there, Jesus went to the regions of Tyre and Sidon. A Canaanite woman from those territories came out and shouted, “Show me mercy, Son of David. My daughter is suffering terribly from demon possession.” But he didn’t respond to her at all.
His disciples came and urged him, “Send her away; she keeps shouting out after us.”
Jesus replied, “I’ve been sent only to the lost sheep, the people of Israel.”
But she knelt before him and said, “Lord, help me.”
He replied, “It is not good to take the children’s bread and toss it to dogs.”
She said, “Yes, Lord. But even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall off their masters’ table.”
Jesus answered, “Woman, you have great faith. It will be just as you wish.” And right then her daughter was healed.

blocks.call: This is the good news of the Lord
blocks.response: Praise to you Lord Jesus Christ

blocks.call: We are the body of Christ
The peace of the Lord be with you

verses: In Christ alone my hope is found
He is my light my strength my song
This Cornerstone this solid Ground
Firm through the fiercest drought and storm
What heights of love what depths of peace
When fears are stilled when strivings cease
My Comforter my All in All
Here in the love of Christ I stand
In Christ alone who took on flesh
Fullness of God in helpless babe
This gift of love and righteousness
Scorned by the ones He came to save
Till on that cross as Jesus died
The wrath of God was satisfied
For every sin on Him was laid
Here in the death of Christ I live
There in the ground His body lay
Light of the world by darkness slain
Then bursting forth in glorious Day
Up from the grave He rose again
And as He stands in victory
Sin’s curse has lost its grip on me
For I am His and He is mine
Bought with the precious blood of Christ
No guilt in life no fear in death
This is the power of Christ in me
From life’s first cry to final breath
Jesus commands my destiny
No power of hell no scheme of man
Can ever pluck me from His hand
Till He returns or calls me home
Here in the power of Christ I’ll stand

lines: Here we gather now at Christ’s table—
a table of justice and freedom.

blocks.response: We lift them to the Lord.

blocks.call: Let us give thanks to the Lord our God.
blocks.response: It is right to give our thanks and praise.

lines: It is right to give you thanks,
You created the world in love,
giving us land, water, people, and purpose.
You called us to live in freedom and community.
You never gave up on us.
You sent prophets to challenge injustice
and show us a better way.
In Jesus, you came among us—
and walking the path of justice.
and called us to live in freedom.
So with all who hunger for freedom,
we give you thanks and praise,
On the night before he died,
Jesus shared a meal with his friends.
This is my body, given for you.
After supper, he took the cup,
This is my blood of the new covenant,
poured out for you and for all,
Let us proclaim the mystery of love.
Jesus died to bring us life.
Jesus rose to bring us hope.
Jesus will come again in love and glory.
so this bread and this wine
may be for us the body and blood of Christ.
make us one with each other,
With your Church across all of creation,
we give you thanks and praise,
Heaven and earth are full of your glory.
Praise to you in the highest.
Father, uphold the holiness of your name.
Give us the bread we need for today.
for we also forgive everyone who has wronged us.
And save us in times of trial.
to receive glory and honour and power,
for Jesus gave himself for us.
In this act of love, we are made whole.
The gifts of God for the people of God.
so that we who try to follow you
may receive food for the journey
with all who walk in your way.

blocks.text: Jesus Christ, Be the Wine of Grace

verses: In the singing, in the silence,
in the hands expectant, open,
in the blessing, in the breaking,
in the presence at this table
Jesus Christ, Jesus Christ,
be the wine of grace.
Jesus Christ, Jesus Christ,
be the bread of peace.
In the question, in the answer,
in the moment of acceptance,
in the heart’s cry, in the healing,
in the circle of your people.
Jesus Christ, Jesus Christ,
be the wine of grace.
Jesus Christ, Jesus Christ,
be the bread of peace.
Amazing grace, how sweet the sound
that saved a wretch like me!
I once was lost, but now am found,
was blind, but now I see.
As grace first taught my heart to fear,
so grace my fears relieved;
how precious did that grace appear,
the hour I first believed!
Through many dangers, toils and snares
I have already come;
God’s grace has brought me safe thus far,
and grace will lead me home.
The Lord has promised good to me,
his word my hope secures;
he will my shield and portion be
as long as life endures.

lines: we thank you for feeding us with grace beyond measure.
Send us out to share this gift freely,
so that all may know your love and salvation.
By the power of your Spirit
keep us always in your love
May the God whose gifts and calling
may the Christ who was argued with at the border
give you a bold and persistent heart;
and may the Spirit who breathes life into all things
send you out to widen the table.
And the blessing of God almighty,
the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit,
be among you and remain with you always.

blocks.call: Go in peace, to love and serve the Lord
blocks.response: In the name of Christ. Amen.

blocks.text: TIS 457 · Sung after the dismissal. Verses 1, 2 and 5. Verses 3 and 4 omitted.

verses: The church’s one foundation
is Jesus Christ her Lord:
she is his new creation
by water and the word;
from heaven he came and sought her
to be his holy bride;
with his own blood he bought her,
and for her life he died.
Elect from every nation,
yet one o’er all the earth,
her charter of salvation
one Lord, one faith, one birth,
one holy name she blesses,
partakes one holy food,
and to one hope she presses,
with every grace endued.
Yet she on earth has union
with God the Three in One,
and mystic sweet communion
with those whose rest is won.
O happy ones and holy!
Lord, give to us grace,
like them, the meek and lowly,
in heaven to seek your face.
